reasons: The cited Section 10(a) contains a genuine Vendor-side defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation in the Customer's favour covering all third-party Claims 'arising out of or in connection with' the Services, the Auction Platform, Vendor's breach of representations/warranties and Vendor's (and its subcontractors') acts or omissions — broad enough to capture IP infringement/misappropriation allegations and Vendor misconduct, with no exclusions or super-cap.

Section 11 supplies the standard indemnity procedure (prompt notice without forfeiture for delay, indemnifying-party control of defence/settlement, no liability-admitting settlement without consent, cooperation at indemnitor's cost), matching the preferred position's procedural element.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact: the clause uses a broad subject-matter trigger rather than the words 'infringe' or 'intellectual property'; substantively IP claims connected with the Services/Platform are within scope, so this is not a rule failure.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed; the rationale correctly notes the two shortfalls (broader Customer-side indemnity in 10(b) and the 'to the best of its knowledge' qualifier on the Creative limb) as sub-preferred points for leverage rather than material deviations, which matches the playbook's classification semantics.
